]]> France’s Airbus A321 MPA faces €12bn cost row, putting 2026 launch at risk https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/france-a321-mpa-maritime-patrol-airbus-cost-dispute/ Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:28:00 +0000 https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/?p=57367 France’s A321 MPA maritime patrol programme faces cost disputes that could push spending toward €12 billion for 12 aircraft, delaying its 2026 development start.

The post France’s Airbus A321 MPA faces €12bn cost row, putting 2026 launch at risk appeared first on AGN.

]]> France’s plan to replace its ageing maritime patrol aircraft with a military version of the Airbus A321XLR has run into a major funding dispute, with the cost of the programme potentially approaching €12 billion ($13 billion) for just 12 aircraft, according to French newspaper Les Echos.

The newspaper reported on 16 November that the A321 MPA programme, intended to replace the French Navy’s Dassault Atlantique 2 fleet, would not enter its development phase this year because of rising costs.

The disclosure follows warnings from French lawmakers that the programme’s estimated budget had already increased by 65%, from €2.768 billion ($3 billion) to €4.574 billion ($5 billion), before a production contract had been signed.

The figures have raised questions about whether France can afford the aircraft in its proposed configuration and still meet the navy’s replacement timetable.

The French Ministry of the Armed Forces acknowledged the problem during an October parliamentary hearing, confirming that negotiations with Airbus were continuing after officials rejected the financial proposals received from industry.

A report to the National Assembly on the 2027 defence budget also confirmed that the programme had been suspended because no agreement had been reached on the financial envelope for the 12 aircraft.

The $13 billion figure reported by Les Echos is not a signed contract value. It includes substantial development and integration expenditure, and the precise scope differs from the earlier budget estimates.

French lawmakers raise concerns

The scale of the dispute was already apparent in October.

In his report on the French Navy’s 2027 budget, lawmaker Yannick Chenevard said the planned launch of the A321 MPA development phase by the end of 2026 was in jeopardy.

The report, registered with the National Assembly on 22 October, stated that technical risk-reduction work had been successful but commercial negotiations had encountered difficulties over Airbus’s financial demands.

Chenevard suggested that Airbus’s approach to pricing might reflect its experience with cost overruns on the A400M military transport programme. That was his assessment, rather than an explanation confirmed by Airbus.

The Ministry of the Armed Forces subsequently addressed the issue during a Senate hearing in the week of 26 October.

Responding to concerns about the delay, the ministry said the estimates received at the end of the summer were unsatisfactory and that France’s defence procurement agency, the Direction generale de l’armement (DGA), was continuing discussions with Airbus.

The ministry also said the Atlantique 2 fleet would remain operational until its replacement arrived, which it placed around 2035.

Why France chose the A321

The A321 MPA emerged from the collapse of a planned Franco-German effort to develop a common maritime patrol aircraft.

France and Germany launched the Maritime Airborne Warfare System (MAWS) initiative in 2018 to replace their ageing maritime patrol fleets.

Germany subsequently chose Boeing’s P-8A Poseidon, ordering five aircraft in 2021 and later increasing its planned fleet to eight.

That decision left France pursuing its own replacement programme.

Two French industrial proposals were considered: an Airbus aircraft based on the A321XLR commercial jet and a Dassault Aviation design derived from the Falcon 10X business jet.

France selected the Airbus proposal for further development, with the larger airliner offering more internal space for mission equipment, weapons and additional crew members during extended patrols.

The choice was particularly important because the new aircraft would have to undertake anti-submarine warfare, maritime surveillance and intelligence missions while also supporting the protection of France’s nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines.

Those submarines form the sea-based element of the country’s nuclear deterrent. Maritime patrol aircraft help monitor the waters through which they transit when departing their bases, looking for hostile submarines and other potential threats.

The A321 MPA was therefore conceived as considerably more than a conventional surveillance aircraft.

Airbus set out its plans in 2025

In February 2025, Airbus Defence and Space announced that the DGA had awarded it a 24-month risk-assessment study contract, with Thales as its industrial partner.

The contract followed an earlier architecture and feasibility study launched at the end of 2022. Airbus said the new work would refine the aircraft’s technical configuration, examine industrial and economic conditions and undertake initial wind-tunnel testing.

The objective was to prepare the programme for a development and production decision at the end of 2026.

Jean-Brice Dumont, then Airbus Defence and Space’s Executive Vice President and Head of Air Power, described the A321 MPA as a potential “true flying frigate”.

“Airbus offers a sovereign solution that provides the autonomy, availability and reliability required to contribute to the oceanic component of the nuclear deterrence,” he said in the February 2025 announcement.

The proposed aircraft would use the A321XLR as its base but require extensive modifications to carry out military missions.
Airbus outlined plans for a maritime surveillance radar with active antennas, acoustic systems to process information from active and passive sonobuoys, electronic and electro-optical sensors, magnetic anomaly detection equipment and self-protection systems.

The aircraft would also carry torpedoes and France’s future anti-ship missile, alongside satellite communications and other mission equipment.

The integration work is considerably more complex than installing surveillance equipment in an existing passenger aircraft. It involves changes to the aircraft’s internal structure, mission systems and weapons arrangements.

That complexity is now central to the disagreement over development costs.

Could Dassault return?

The financial dispute has also revived questions about the Dassault Falcon 10X proposal, which lost out to Airbus during the earlier selection process.

According to subsequent French reporting, the DGA could consider reopening discussions with both manufacturers if the current negotiations fail to produce an acceptable agreement.

However, no decision to abandon the A321 MPA or select an alternative aircraft has been announced.

A Falcon 10X-based design would still have to satisfy the navy’s requirements for endurance, mission systems, weapons capacity and crew accommodation.

Ageing Atlantique 2 fleet adds urgency

The French Navy currently relies on 18 Atlantique 2 aircraft upgraded to Standard 6.

The twin-turboprop aircraft have served for decades in anti-submarine warfare, maritime surveillance and other naval operations.

Their latest modernisation programme introduced improved sensors and mission systems, extending their usefulness while France develops a replacement.

The Ministry of the Armed Forces told senators in October that the final major upgrade had been completed and that all 18 aircraft had received new sensors.

The post Türkiye first nation to field uncrewed fighter jets as three Kızılelmas enter service appeared first on AGN.

]]> The Turkish Armed Forces have taken delivery of their first three Bayraktar Kızılelma wingman drones today, 19 November, putting an uncrewed fighter jet into service before any other country in the world.

Baykar announced the handover from Çorlu in northwestern Türkiye, where much of Kızılelma’s flight testing took place. The manufacturer said all three aircraft had passed their acceptance tests and entered active service.

President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan welcomed the arrival.

“Today is a historic day on which a great dream has become a reality,” he wrote on social media. “Our Bayraktar Kızılelma unmanned combat aircraft has been inducted into the inventory of the Turkish Armed Forces after years of work and tremendous effort.”

Baykar hands over three Kızılelma fighter drones after 600 test and training sorties

Less than four years separate the handover from Kızılelma’s maiden flight on December 14, 2022. Baykar financed the aircraft’s development itself and says the program has since accumulated 600 test and training sorties. The company describes the delivery as the first time an uncrewed fighter jet has entered operational service anywhere in the world.

The world’s first operational Unmanned Combat Aircraft, has been delivered to the Turkish military. Today, Türkiye officially inducted its first unmanned combat aircraft (two of them), the Bayraktar KIZILELMA, into service following successful acceptance tests. Developed by Baykar, KIZILELMA is designed for air-to-air and air-to-ground missions. It has already demonstrated its ability to engage jet-powered aerial targets using the indigenous GÖKDOĞAN beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile and ASELSAN’s MURAD AESA radar. Türkiye has now become the first country to officially field an unmanned fighter aircraft.

— Comandante🎖️ (@commandante_) November 19, 2026

Designed for both air combat and strikes against surface targets, Kızılelma measures 14.5 meters long and has a wingspan of 10 meters. Its credentials as a fighter were put to the test in November 2025, when a prototype flew out over the Black Sea near Sinop. Using a Turkish-built MURAD radar, the aircraft engaged a jet-powered target with a Gökdoğan beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile and scored a direct hit, according to Baykar.

A trial at Çorlu this May showed how the aircraft can interact with crewed assets. After taking off autonomously, Kızılelma joined a Leonardo M-346 in the air. The pilots aboard the Italian-built jet then took control of the formation, directing the drone to change position, break away and rejoin while an Italian Air Force trainer flew chase.

The M-346 crew decided where it wanted its wingman. Kızılelma worked out how to fly there.

How far has the rest of the world come with their own drone wingmen?

With the handover of the first three Kızılelma jets, Türkiye has claimed a place in aviation history. Baykar says it is the first country to bring an uncrewed fighter jet into active service. But it’s not the only nation that is attempting to.

The US Air Force already has two contenders in the air. General Atomics’ FQ-42 Vengeance and Anduril’s FQ-44 Fury both won production contracts in June, and the service has assigned aircraft to its Experimental Operations Unit at Creech Air Force Base in Nevada. On October 8, an F-22 pilot directed a Fury in flight. Later that month, two US collaborative combat aircraft flew coordinated air combat manoeuvres during a test.

Australia, meanwhile, got into the air earlier than either country’s current designs. Boeing’s MQ-28 Ghost Bat first flew in February 2021, nearly two years before Kızılelma. In December 2025, a Ghost Bat teamed with a Royal Australian Air Force E-7A Wedgetail and an F/A-18F Super Hornet to destroy an airborne target during trials at Woomera. Canberra has committed about A$1.4 billion ($935 M) to collaborative air capabilities, including bringing Ghost Bat into operational service.

The UK has taken a different route. Its Royal Air Force already fields StormShroud, an electronic warfare drone, while StormFighter is the closer British counterpart to Kızılelma. The RAF launched StormFighter in July under a wider £300 million investment in collaborative combat aircraft. Ministers have outlined a role alongside crewed combat jets, although no public invitation to tender for StormFighter itself has yet emerged.

The next question for Türkiye is one the handover leaves open. Baykar has shown that Kızılelma can take instructions from a crewed jet, and the armed forces now have three aircraft of their own. How Turkish crews will use them, and which fighters they will fly alongside, has yet to be announced.

 SIE Custom Header — v1.1.2
 Zero-CLS, no JavaScript layout shifts.
 No panoramic image — lean 64px nav bar only.
 backdrop-filter is intentionally NOT used on .sie-hdr__bar.
 Any element with backdrop-filter becomes a CSS containing block for
 position:fixed descendants, which would trap the user-ui mobile bottom bar
 (position:fixed; bottom:0) inside the header instead of the viewport.
 ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
/* ── Root variables ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
:root {
 --sie-hdr-brand:       #0056b3;        /* SIE brand blue                      */
 --sie-hdr-brand-light: #1a6fc4;
 --sie-hdr-bar-h:       64px;           /* nav bar height — fixed, prevents CLS */
 /* 2026-11-08: bar moved from bright brand blue (#0056b3) to the navy the
 homepage redesign uses (#12233D), so header, hero and institutions band

 --sie-hdr-bar-bg:      #12233D;        /* solid — no backdrop-filter needed   */
 --sie-hdr-bar-border:  rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
}
/* ── Wrapper ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr {
 width: 100%;
 display: block;
 min-height: var(--sie-hdr-bar-h);
 /* Own stacking context so dropdowns render above Divi page content */
 position: relative;
 z-index: 1000;
}
/* ── Navigation bar ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__bar {
 height: var(--sie-hdr-bar-h);
 background: var(--sie-hdr-bar-bg);
 /* NO backdrop-filter here — it would trap position:fixed children
 (user-ui mobile bottom bar) inside this element instead of viewport */
 border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sie-hdr-bar-border);
}
.sie-hdr__inner {
 max-width: 1280px;
 height: 100%;
 margin: 0 auto;
 padding: 0 24px;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 32px;
}
/* ── Logo ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__logo {
 flex-shrink: 0;
 text-decoration: none;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
}
.sie-hdr__logo-img {
 height: 54px;
 width: auto;
 display: block;
}
.sie-hdr__logo-text {
 font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
 font-size: 17px;
 font-weight: 700;
 color: #fff;
 letter-spacing: -0.01em;
 white-space: nowrap;
}
/* ── Desktop navigation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__nav {
 flex: 1;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list {
 list-style: none;
 margin: 0;
 padding: 0;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list li {
 position: relative;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list a,
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {
 display: inline-flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
 padding: 8px 14px;
 font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
 font-size: 14px;
 font-weight: 500;
 color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
 text-decoration: none;
 border-radius: 8px;
 transition: background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease;
 white-space: nowrap;
 min-height: 48px; /* WCAG touch target */
}
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {
 background: none;
 border: none;
 cursor: pointer;
}
.sie-hdr__nav-list a:hover,
.sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle:hover,
.sie-hdr__has-dropdown:hover > .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12);
 color: #fff;
}
/* ── Resources dropdown ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__dropdown {
 display: none;
 position: absolute;
 top: calc(100% + 6px);
 left: 0;
 min-width: 240px;
 background: #fff;
 border-radius: 12px;
 box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18);
 padding: 8px 0;
 list-style: none;
 margin: 0;
 z-index: 9999;
}

@media (hover: hover) {

 }
}

}

 margin: 0;
 padding: 0;
}

 font-weight: 500;
 border-radius: 0;
 min-height: unset;

.sie-hdr__has-dropdown:hover .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle svg {
 transform: rotate(180deg);
}
/* ── Mobile hamburger ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr__hamburger {
 display: none;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: center;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 5px;

 height: 44px;
 background: none;
 border: none;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 0;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 margin-left: auto;

 width: 22px;
 height: 2px;
 background: #fff;
 border-radius: 2px;
 transition: transform 0.25s ease, opacity 0.25s ease;

}
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(2) {
 opacity: 0;
}
.sie-hdr__hamburger[aria-expanded="true"] span:nth-child(3) {
 transform: translateY(-7px) rotate(-45deg);
}

 user-ui.php's desktop bar uses position:absolute; top:20px; right:30px — that
 was designed for Divi's header context. Inside our flex .sie-hdr__inner we
 need it as a normal flex child instead.
 Fixed-position children (auth drawer, mobile bar, destinations panel) are
 unaffected — position:fixed is always viewport-relative provided no ancestor

 three on .sie-hdr__bar).
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.sie-hdr .se-user-menu-wrapper {
 position: static !important;
 top: auto !important;
 right: auto !important;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 margin-left: auto;
}

@media (max-width: 860px) {

 display: none !important;
 }
}

 user-ui's default .se-ai-icon is 86×86 px (fine for the mobile bottom bar),

 height: 36px !important;

.sie-hdr .se-dest-desktop-btn,

.sie-hdr .se-shortlist-link:hover,
.sie-hdr .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover,
.sie-hdr .se-user-icon:hover {

.sie-hdr .se-fav-desktop-link:hover {

 }

 }
 .sie-hdr__nav {

 top: var(--sie-hdr-bar-h);           /* flush below the nav bar */

 right: 0;

 }

 }
 .sie-hdr__nav-list {

 align-items: flex-start;
 gap: 0;
 padding: 0 16px;
 }
 .sie-hdr__nav-list a,
 .sie-hdr__dropdown-toggle {

 .sie-hdr__dropdown {

 .lh-heroalt{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:10px;min-width:0}

 /* ── Make the search the priority, not an afterthought ────────────────
 Measured before this change at 1440x900: hero 1028px tall, search bar
 top at y=694. Tightened the vertical rhythm and moved the trust row

 .lh-hero.lh-hero{padding:clamp(28px,4vw,56px) 0 clamp(32px,4.5vw,64px)}
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-center{gap:clamp(16px,2vw,26px)}
 /* ⚠️ THE CAUSE OF THE BIG EMPTY GAP, and it was mine. The stylesheet sets
 .lh-hero-text{flex:1 1 380px} and .lh-portals{flex:1 1 420px}. Those were
 written for the original ROW layout, where flex-basis is a WIDTH. Turning
 the container into a column silently turned both into fixed HEIGHTS: the
 text box stayed 380px tall although its content ended after 187px, and
 the search row stayed 420px tall although the cards are 195px. That is
 ~420px of enforced emptiness. Resetting the basis is the whole fix —
 never set flex-direction on an inherited flex container without checking
 what flex-basis meant before. */
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{margin-bottom:10px}
 .lh-hero .lh-title{margin:0 0 12px}
 .lh-hero .lh-subtitle{margin:0;max-width:52ch}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{position:relative;z-index:1;margin:clamp(14px,1.8vw,22px) 0 0;gap:10px 24px}
 /* The bar itself carries the emphasis: taller, larger type, and a navy

 paper it was the loudest thing in the hero. Scoped to .lh-herosearch so
 the same widget elsewhere keeps the brand button. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-bar{min-height:64px;padding:4px 6px 4px 14px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-input{font-size:17px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn{background:#12233D;border-color:#12233D;color:#fff;font-weight:600}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn:hover{background:#1E3354;border-color:#1E3354}
 /* ── Results as a responsive grid, not a single strip ──────────────────
 .sie-res-list holds the program cards as direct children (verified live:
 18 cards, one parent, no headers in between), so one grid rule is enough.
 ⚠️ SCOPED TO THE HOMEPAGE ON PURPOSE. .sie-res-list is the shared
 SieFlowView markup — Leonardo renders into it too, with its own
 per-card animation offsets. Re-layouting it globally would change his
 results as a side effect of a homepage fix. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(320px,1fr));gap:16px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list > .program-card{width:auto;max-width:none;margin:0}
 /* The flow view (AI matching on) groups results into one .sie-flow__branch

 two never fit and they stack — the "single strip". Releasing the cap and
 tiling the branches gives two country panels per row at this width, and
 more on a wider screen, without touching the cards inside.
 ⚠️ Scoped to .lh-herosearch: Leonardo renders the same flow markup. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(360px,1fr));gap:18px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branch{max-width:none;width:100%}
 /* ── The figures strip ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Serif numerals, monospaced labels, hairline rules, no card, no shadow,
 no colour fill behind each figure. The register of a register. */
 .lh-stats.lh-stats--figures{background:#F4F2ED;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8;padding:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr));gap:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat{padding:clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) clamp(14px,2vw,28px) clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) 0;border-right:1px solid #E4E0D8;text-align:left;background:none;border-radius:0;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:last-child{border-right:0}
 /* Every cell except the first gets inner space on its left, so each rule
 sits with equal air on both sides instead of crowding the next figure.
 The first keeps padding-left:0 so its numeral lines up with the margin
 the hero headline uses. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat + .lh-stat{padding-left:clamp(18px,2.4vw,34px)}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-num{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(27px,2.9vw,40px);font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;line-height:1.05;color:#12233D;background:none;-webkit-text-fill-color:currentColor}
 /* #6B7A8D measured 3.92:1 against the warm band — under the 4.5:1 that
 11.5px text needs. The cool grey was fine on the old cold background and
 quietly failed when the palette warmed up; #4F5967 measures 6.2:1.
 Worth remembering when warming any other background. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-label{margin-top:8px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.3px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#4F5967}
 @media(max-width:700px){
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:nth-child(2){border-right:0}
 }

 .lh-inst{background:#12233D;color:#fff}

 .lh-inst-badge{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-h{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(26px,3.1vw,40px);line-height:1.16;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;color:#fff;max-width:20ch}
 .lh-inst-body{margin:0 0 26px;font-size:clamp(15.5px,1.4vw,17px);line-height:1.65;color:#C6D2E0;max-width:54ch}

 /* ── Institutional pass, part 2 (2026-11-08, evening) ──────────────────
 Brings the sections below the hero onto the palette and type the hero
 already uses, so the page reads as one document instead of two designs
 stacked on top of each other. Everything here is homepage-only (it lives
 in this template) and is pure CSS: delete this block to revert. */
 /* The page itself: the site-wide body is cold pale blue (#E8F1FA), which
 showed through every transparent section (the institutions carousel and
 the study fields block) as a blue band between warm ones. */
 body.page-id-150{background:#FAF8F4}
 /* ⚠️ THE HEADLINE NEVER WAS SERIF. leonardo-homepage-css.min.css carries
 `.lh-wrap .lh-title{font-family:system-ui !important; font-size:44px
 !important; font-weight:800 !important; color:#003b73 !important}`, so
 the Source Serif rule earlier in this block lost on every device. Only
 !important with equal-or-higher specificity can beat it. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title,.lh-wrap .lh-hero h2.lh-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(34px,4.4vw,58px) !important;line-height:1.08 !important;letter-spacing:-.6px !important;color:#12233D !important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D !important}
 /* The accent word: italic navy reads editorial; bright orange read promo. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-gradient-text{color:#12233D;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D;font-style:italic;font-weight:600}
 /* One label above the headline is enough. The H1 eyebrow ("STUDY IN
 EUROPE") already does that job; the extra pill only added noise. */
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{display:none}
 /* Phones: the hero had no side gutter, so the eyebrow sat flush against
 the screen edge while the centred text did not. Left-aligned, with the
 same 20px gutter as the rest of the page, it matches the desktop. */
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-center{padding-left:20px;padding-right:20px;box-sizing:border-box;text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text,.lh-hero .lh-subtitle{text-align:left}
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title{text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 }
 /* ── Section headers: same voice as the institutions band ─────────────
 Serif headings and a small monospaced label instead of the rounded blue
 pills, which were the last "app" element on the page. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-header h2{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px) !important;letter-spacing:-.4px;line-height:1.15;color:#12233D !important}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-badge{display:inline-block;margin-bottom:14px;padding:0;background:none;border-radius:0;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8C5A23}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-sub{color:#4A525C}
 /* Section rhythm: paper / white / paper, so each block has an edge. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-how{background:#FAF8F4}
 .lh-wrap .lh-unis{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 /* How it works: the three steps were top-aligned, so the middle card
 (longer text) hung lower than its neighbours. Stretch evens them. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-steps{align-items:stretch}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step{background:#fff;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}

 .lh-wrap .lh-step-arrow{color:#B7B1A5}

 /* ── Study fields block (rendered by [sie_study_fields] after .lh-wrap) ─

 the loudest part of the page. Same content, one navy, warm neutrals.
 The branch colours arrive as INLINE custom properties and inline
 backgrounds, so these overrides need !important to apply. Scoped to the
 homepage: the study-field pages keep their colour coding. */
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px);letter-spacing:-.4px;color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-subtitle{color:#4A525C}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__source-pill{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;box-shadow:none !important;border-radius:4px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__junction-dot{background:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch{--branch-color:#12233D !important;--branch-bg:#F4F2ED !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-accent{display:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-icon{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-count{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card{background:#FAF8F4;border:1px solid #EDEAE3;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card:hover{border-color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-icon{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__leo-link{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leonardo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leo-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px}
 /* Alignment: the search widget carries its own 24px side padding, so the
 bar sat indented from the headline above it; and the trust row was
 centred under a left-aligned column. Both now share the text's edge.
 Only the LEFT padding goes: removing the right one too pushed the
 "AI-enhanced matching" toggle across the seam into the navy side. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-wrap{padding-left:0 !important}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 /* Institution cards: the stylesheet tints each card top a different pastel
 (blue / yellow / blue) via !important rules at .lh-uni-card:nth-child()
 specificity, so this needs one more class to win. Plain paper, so the
 monogram or logo is the only thing that differs between cards. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card:nth-child(n) .lh-uni-card-top{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-bottom:1px solid #EDEAE3}
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-cta{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 .lh-wrap .sie-dest-hub__name{color:#12233D}

 DESTINATIONS PANEL  — overlay + grid
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
 /* Outer layer: covers full viewport */
 .sie-dest-panel {
 position: fixed;
 inset: 0;
 z-index: 2147483000;
 display: flex;
 align-items: stretch;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 opacity: 0;
 visibility: hidden;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .25s ease, visibility .25s;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open {
 opacity: 1;
 visibility: visible;
 pointer-events: auto;
 }
 /* Backdrop */
 .sie-dest-panel__backdrop {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 background: rgba(11, 55, 112, .52);
 backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 cursor: pointer;
 }
 /* Sheet — right-panel on desktop */
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 position: relative;
 z-index: 1;
 width: min(800px, 100%);
 height: 100%;
 background: #fff;
 overflow-y: auto;
 -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
 padding: 26px 26px 40px;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 gap: 0;
 transform: translateX(28px);
 opacity: 0;
 transition: transform .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), opacity .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
 box-shadow: -20px 0 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateX(0);
 opacity: 1;
 }
 /* Mobile: bottom-sheet */
 @media (max-width: 767px) {
 .sie-dest-panel {
 align-items: flex-end;
 justify-content: stretch;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 width: 100%;
 height: 92vh;
 border-top-left-radius: 22px;
 border-top-right-radius: 22px;
 padding: 20px 16px 40px;
 transform: translateY(28px);
 box-shadow: 0 -16px 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateY(0);
 }
 }
 /* ── Header ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__header {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 justify-content: space-between;
 margin-bottom: 6px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__titlewrap {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 10px;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__globe {
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #1e66f5;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__title {
 font-size: 1.5rem;
 font-weight: 800;
 color: #0b3770;
 margin: 0;
 line-height: 1.2;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close {
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #0b3770;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 6px 8px;
 border-radius: 8px;
 line-height: 1;
 opacity: .75;
 transition: opacity .15s, background .15s;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close:hover {
 opacity: 1;
 background: #f0f4ff;
 }
 /* Subheading */
 .sie-dest-panel__sub {
 color: #466087;
 font-size: .94rem;
 margin: 0 0 20px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 /* ── Country grid ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 display: grid;
 grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
 gap: 14px;
 /* allow this to grow and scroll */
 flex: 1;
 align-content: start;
 }
 @media (max-width: 620px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
 gap: 10px;
 }
 }
 @media (min-width: 621px) and (max-width: 860px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
 }
 }
 /* ── Country card ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__card {
 position: relative;
 display: block;
 aspect-ratio: 3 / 2;
 border-radius: 12px;
 overflow: hidden;
 text-decoration: none;
 background: #1d3557;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card--no-img .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1d3557 0%, #1e66f5 100%);
 }
 /* Hero image layer — scales on hover */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 transition: transform .4s ease;
 will-change: transform;
 }
 /* <img> fills the card exactly like background-size:cover did.
 loading="lazy" means the browser only fetches each image when the
 panel opens and the card enters the viewport — saving ~30 MB of
 upfront image requests on every page that includes this panel. */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-img {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 width: 100%;
 height: 100%;
 object-fit: cover;
 object-position: center;
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-bg,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 transform: scale(1.07);
 }
 /* Gradient overlay + text */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-body {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 padding: 10px 12px 10px;
 background: linear-gradient(
 to top,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .72) 0%,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .30) 55%,
 transparent 100%
 );
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-name {
 color: #fff;
 font-weight: 700;
 font-size: .92rem;
 line-height: 1.2;
 text-shadow: 0 1px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 display: block;
 color: rgba(255,255,255,0);
 font-size: .75rem;
 margin-top: 2px;
 transition: color .2s ease, transform .2s ease;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 color: rgba(255,255,255,.9);
 transform: translateX(4px);
 }
 /* ── Body-scroll lock ── */
 body.sie-dest-panel-open {
 overflow: hidden;
 }
 /* ── Country interest heart ── */
 .sie-country-heart {
 position: absolute;
 top: 8px;
 right: 8px;
 z-index: 10;
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
 border: none;
 border-radius: 20px;
 padding: 4px 8px 4px 7px;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
 cursor: pointer;
 font-size: 13px;
 color: #94a3b8;
 box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.22);
 backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 transition: color .18s, transform .18s, background .18s;
 line-height: 1;
 min-width: 28px;
 justify-content: center;
 }
 .sie-country-heart:hover {
 transform: scale(1.12);
 background: #fff;
 color: #ef4444;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted {
 color: #ef4444;
 background: #fff;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted i {
 animation: sie-heart-pop .35s cubic-bezier(.36,.07,.19,.97);
 }
 @keyframes sie-heart-pop {
 0%   { transform: scale(1); }
 40%  { transform: scale(1.45); }
 70%  { transform: scale(.88); }
 100% { transform: scale(1); }
 }
 .sie-country-heart__count {
 font-size: 11px;
 font-weight: 700;
 color: inherit;
 display: none;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.has-votes .sie-country-heart__count {
 display: inline;
 }
 /* ── Trigger button styles (for use in any menu) ── */
 /* Desktop globe icon */
 .se-dest-desktop-btn {
 font-size: 24px;
 color: #fff;
 text-decoration: none;
 cursor: pointer;
 transition: transform .2s, color .2s;
 position: relative;
 line-height: 1;
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 padding: 0;
 }
 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover {
 transform: scale(1.15);
 color: #FFCC00;
 }
 /* Tooltip on desktop */
 @media (min-width: 1024px) {
 .se-dest-desktop-btn::after {
 content: "Study Destinations";
 position: absolute;
 bottom: -30px;
 left: 50%;
 transform: translateX(-50%);
 background: #007BFF;
 color: #fff;
 padding: 4px 8px;
 font-size: 12px;
 border-radius: 5px;
 opacity: 0;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .2s;
 white-space: nowrap;
 }
 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover::after {
 opacity: 1;
 }
 }
 /* Mobile pill button */
 .se-dest-btn {
 background: #0b3770 !important;
 color: #fff !important;
 }
 .se-dest-btn:hover {
 background: #1e66f5 !important;

<h1 class="title-h1 eac-page-title">Conference on the Future of Europe : the future is in your hands</h1>
<span><span>sandoel</span></span>
<span><time datetime="2021-12-07T08:55:30+01:00" title="Tuesday, December 7, 2021 - 08:55">Tue, 12/07/2021 - 08:55</time>
</span>
<div class="ecl"><h2><strong>What is the Conference?</strong></h2>

<p>The <strong>Conference on the Future of Europe </strong>is the first transnational discussion with Europeans on how to address Europe’s challenges together. This is an opportunity to think about what citizens and&nbsp; civil society want for the European Union.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
</div>

  </article>

                                                                <div class="video-description lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><div><p>The European Parliament, the Council, and the European Commission have committed to listen and follow up on the recommendations made</p></div></div>

<div class="lc-padding-top-half lc-padding-bottom-default lc-background-color-white lc-contained eac-stripe eac-stripe--bg-white" id="paragraph-827">  <div class="eac-stripe__inner">            <div class="full-html-body">
  <div class="eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><h2><strong>How does the Conference work?</strong></h2>

<p>Europeans can share ideas via the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Multilingual Digital Platform</a>, and both national and&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/assemblies/citizens-panels" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">European Citizens' Panels</a>. These contributions feed into the&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/plenary" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference Plenaries</a>.</p>

<p>The Conference&nbsp;offers a new public forum for an open, inclusive, and transparent debate with citizens around a number of key priorities and challenges.</p>

<h2><strong>How can you participate?</strong></h2>

<ul>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]--><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/processes?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">share your own ideas or support others’ ideas</a> on the multilingual digital Conference platform</li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->organise your own events and promote it by adding them to the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference platform</a></li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->take a look at the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/meetings" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">events organised by people across the EU</a></li>
</ul>

<h2><strong>What will the outcome be?</strong></h2>

<p>All of the ideas gathered and reports on events are published on the platform openly and transparently. These reports will then directly influence the discussions in the European Citizens’ Panels as well as in the Plenaries, where citizens will enter into a dialogue with national and European decision makers.</p>

<p>By spring 2022, the Conference will provide guidance on the future of Europe to the European institutions</p>

<p><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/getinvolved" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Get involved and make your voice heard when it comes to education, culture, youth, sport, and more</a>.</p>

<p>Follow on Twitter at&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
	<li><a class="external-link eac-external-link" href="https://twitter.com/search?q=%23TheFutureIsYours" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">#TheFutureIsYours</a></li>
	<li><a href="https://twitter.com/search?q=%23#FutureofEurope" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">#FutureofEurope</a></li>
</ul>

Restaurants are where people come together over good food. We build the technology that keeps them running.

CodeRabbit is the governance and control layer for agentic software development, helping engineering teams trust the code they ship. Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation, and growth drives everything we do. Our Brand & Experience team builds the emotional connection between Deliveroo and our customers, riders, and partners. With a deep understanding of our audience and a passion for creativity, we bring our brand to life across every touchpoint. Whether it's a push notification, social campaign, or packaging design—we craft compelling experiences that shape perceptions, spark engagement, and make Deliveroo a loved, global brand.

We're looking for a Senior Marketing Manager, Brand Integrated Marketing to join our London team. This is a hybrid role. In this role, you'll help us take ideas from global strategy through to local activation across markets, delivering integrated campaigns that drive measurable business growth.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll be joining the Integrated Marketing team. We own the Deliveroo brand globally and lead our biggest campaign moments. Working in a cross-functional squad alongside strategic teams, functional leads, and local markets, we turn big ideas into high-impact campaigns across our markets.

Here's what your day-to-day might look like:

  • Global Campaign Ownership: Lead high-profile global marketing programmes and integrated campaigns from global strategy through to local market execution.

  • Framework & Playbook Development: Design, scale, and maintain measurement frameworks, playbooks, and systems that enable global and local teams to execute best-in-class brand campaigns.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner closely with cross-functional squads, strategic teams, functional leads, and local market leads to align campaign strategies with core business goals.

  • Stakeholder Management: Influence senior stakeholders across the global organisation without direct authority, ensuring alignment on messaging, execution, and performance metrics.

  • Strategic Optimisation: Balance tactical execution with a longer-term strategic perspective to solve complex marketing briefs and continuously optimize brand performance.

What You'll Need to Thrive

Essential

  • Integrated Brand Leadership: Proven experience leading end-to-end global integrated marketing campaigns from initial strategy through to local market activation.

  • Framework Development: Strong track record in establishing measurement frameworks, campaign playbooks, and operational systems that scale across multiple regions.

  • Stakeholder Influence: Demonstrated ability to influence and align senior cross-functional stakeholders and matrix teams without direct line management authority.

  • Strategic & Tactical Execution: Proven ability to operate independently on complex or ambiguous briefs, balancing day-to-day execution with longer-term brand strategy.

  • Commercial Acumen: Strong expertise in linking brand initiatives and marketing campaigns directly to measurable business growth and commercial impact.

Nice to Have

  • Experience navigating three-sided marketplace dynamics or fast-paced consumer tech environments.

  • Background working across international or multi-market structures.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving.

We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

🔧 Make a visible impact every day

Your work directly improves experiences for customers, partners and riders.

🌱 Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment

Work close to the market with autonomy, pace and real responsibility.

🧠 Build a career, not just a role

Stretch yourself, develop new skills and grow as the business evolves.

🌎 Deliver together in an inclusive culture

Collaborative, values-driven teams that support how you work best.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find more about how we hire here.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!


Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

SingleStore is looking for an accomplished sales professional to join our Sales Team. AI is moving from experimentation into production, and this role is an opportunity to break into AI while doing meaningful enterprise selling.

As an Account Executive, AI Hunter, your job is simple: create new SingleStore customers. You will find companies building AI applications where data access, real-time context, memory, retrieval, or operational scale is becoming a constraint—and turn those challenges into new SingleStore customers. You will own a broad territory, build a majority self-sourced pipeline, create demand in an emerging category, and close greenfield enterprise opportunities.

This is a true hunting role. You will engage customers before they have a defined project, develop customer-specific points of view, create urgency around business and technical problems, work with technical experts to land first production workloads, and build a measurable new-logo business with broad ownership. The ideal candidate is a measurable enterprise hunter who is competitive, curious, technically credible, resilient, and able to sell business outcomes. Direct AI sales experience is valuable, but proven selling ability and technical curiosity matter more than a narrow "AI seller" title.

Role and Responsibilities

  • Build and execute a territory strategy for net-new customer acquisition.
  • Prospect fearlessly across a broad account universe using proactive, persistent outbound, account-based, partner, and market-education motions; stay resilient and effective through rejection and ambiguity.
  • Form account hypotheses, map the buying center, and earn first meetings with relevant points of view tailored to the customer.
  • Engage executive, business, technical, security, and procurement stakeholders.
  • Lead great business-first discovery, connect AI and data challenges to fundable goals, and build quantified ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases.
  • Build and develop champions, multi-thread the buying group, earn executive and economic-buyer access, and maintain stakeholder alignment; own the stakeholder plan, mutual action plan, close plan, value case, stage gates, forecast, and commercial outcome.
  • Lead complex sales cycles through technical validation, security, legal, procurement, negotiation, and close.
  • Partner with Solutions and Forward Deployment Engineers and cross-functional teams to validate technical fit and establish the first production workload.
  • Navigate competitive displacement and maintain disciplined activity management, CRM hygiene, reporting, qualification, forecasting, and opportunity management; showcase clear metrics such as pipeline created, meetings, conversion, quota attainment, and new-logo performance.
  • Be AI fluent: use AI and research tools productively and responsibly while applying judgment, validating outputs, and separating facts from hypotheses.
  • Travel within the assigned territory as required. 

Required Skills and Experience

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying B2B enterprise software sales experience, ideally selling to large or technically sophisticated organizations; experience in data, cloud, analytics, AI, or adjacent technical domains is a plus.
  • Repeated, quantified quota success with clear ownership of new-logo wins and self-sourced pipeline.
  • Experience closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals involving executives, technical evaluators, security, legal, finance, procurement, and partners.
  • Ability to sell measurable business outcomes and build ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases.
  • Technical fluency in an adjacent domain such as databases, data infrastructure, analytics, AI/ML, cloud, Kubernetes, developer tools, cybersecurity, observability, or open-source software.
  • Strong qualification, account planning, forecasting, CRM, negotiation, and deal-management skills.
  • Learning velocity and coachability, demonstrated through specific behavior change after feedback; ability to explain technical concepts clearly to technical and executive audiences.
  • Executive presence, customer trust, resilience, intellectual honesty, and excellent communication skills.
  • B.A., B.S. degree or equivalent in a related field.
  • Experience with Fortune 500 or security-sensitive organizations, cloud ecosystems, open-source or consumption-based products, or emerging categories is preferred.

About the role

LemFi's Foundations tribe is the platform backbone every product team relies on. We own onboarding and identity (KYC end-to-end), engagement systems (rewards, CRM tooling, Lemfi cash), and the internal SDKs and architectural standards that let other squads move fast without reinventing the wheel. If it touches how a customer gets onto the platform or how teams build reliably on top of it, it runs through us.
We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer who is at home in Go, cares deeply about building things that last, and has the ownership instinct to drive a system from design to production with minimal hand-holding. You will be a key technical voice in the tribe - setting standards, shipping real product, and enabling the rest of engineering to move faster because of the work you do.

What you'll build and own

  • Own and evolve our core identity and onboarding services - KYC flows, verification orchestration and the data contracts that downstream systems depend on.

  • Build and maintain internal SDKs and shared libraries that abstract platform concerns (auth, identity, caching, eventing) so product teams can move without friction.

  • Define and champion cross-platform architectural standards, making opinionated decisions about service design, API contracts and data consistency that the wider engineering org follows.

  • Drive engagement platform capabilities - rewards logic, CRM integrations and Lemfi cash - from spec to production, using AI-assisted development tooling to compress iteration cycles without sacrificing correctness.

  • Partner closely with platform and infrastructure teams to raise the reliability and observability bar across Foundations-owned services.

  • Tackle the hard, ambiguous problems - new country launches, regulatory identity requirements, scaling events - and turn them into clean, well-documented solutions.

  • Contribute to a high-ownership engineering culture: code reviews, architectural reviews, incident response and mentoring are part of the job, not extras.

Your experience

  • At least five years of backend engineering experience with Go as your primary language in a production environment.

  • A track record of building and scaling distributed systems - you have seen things break at scale and know how to design so they do not.

  • Experience working on or closely with platform or enablement teams: shared libraries, internal tooling, developer experience or API gateways.

  • Comfortable with the full lifecycle - design, build, operate, improve - with evidence of genuine end-to-end ownership rather than handing off to other teams.

  • Practical, demonstrable use of AI development tools in your daily engineering workflow; you validate AI output rather than blindly accepting it.

  • Strong opinions about system design, API contracts and service boundaries, backed by real examples you can walk us through.

Nice to have

  • Exposure to fintech, payments or identity/KYC systems.

  • Experience building SDKs or developer-facing platform services consumed by other engineering teams.

  • Prior work in a high-growth startup or scale-up (roughly 50-500 people) where you had to set standards, not just follow them.


Why join LemFi?

Your work here puts money back into families' pockets. That's the reward, and the weight of it. You'll take on some of the hardest problems in finance alongside people who do their best work when the stakes are real. We move fast and we expect a lot, because our customers can't afford for us to do otherwise. In return you get room to own real problems, global impact you can see, and a team that won't slow you down.

Bring grit and ownership and there's a place for them here. Ambition belongs here, come and show us yours.

About Artificial

Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.

About the role

We're looking for a Senior Product Security Engineer to make our applications, and the platform they run on, secure. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll work inside our engineering teams, review how our platforms are designed, find where they are weak, and help get them fixed.

Much of the job is setting up practices we don't yet have. You'll make threat modelling a normal part of how we plan and build, introduce vulnerability management across our applications and AWS infrastructure, and automate security testing at every stage of the delivery pipeline. We want checks that run on every change, so engineers find problems early and fix them in their own teams without everything having to route through you.

We're investing in AI-assisted engineering across the company, and we have a working group exploring where it helps us build better software. Security is part of that work from the start. You'll join the working group, set the guardrails and automated checks that hold every change to the same standard however it was written, and use the same tools in your own work.

Job responsibilities

  • Make threat modelling a standard part of how engineering plans and builds, run it on the highest-risk work, and train teams to do their own

  • Review the security architecture of our platforms end to end, and turn what you find into prioritised work

  • Set up and run vulnerability management across application code and AWS infrastructure, with a clear severity model and agreed fix times

  • Build automated security testing into every stage of the pipeline, covering secrets scanning, static and dynamic testing and dependency checks, tuned so it catches real problems without getting in the way

  • Run internal penetration testing as a continuing activity, using AI tools to test features as they ship, and coordinate external testing

  • Put AWS security guardrails in place as Terraform, and keep configuration from drifting

  • Set up how we manage and rotate secrets, and build controls for our software supply chain

  • Test that customer data stays properly separated between tenants, and keep production data out of non-production

  • Build the guardrails for agentic engineering, covering what agents can access, how they are sandboxed, which tools and connectors they can use, and the checks agent-written code has to pass before it merges

  • Give engineers practical security advice day to day, and fix issues yourself when that is the fastest way to get them fixed

About you

Skills, experience and qualifications

  • Strong product or application security background built on software engineering experience, and comfortable reading, writing and reviewing code

  • Experience running threat modelling and getting engineering teams to adopt it as their own

  • Experience introducing vulnerability management that engineering teams work to

  • Hands-on with security testing across the pipeline, including secrets scanning, SAST, DAST and SCA, and with tuning those tools to cut noise

  • Experience penetration testing web applications and APIs

  • Good working knowledge of AWS security, including access and identity, networking and encryption, and able to read, review and write Terraform

  • Use AI coding agents in your daily work, and can show security tooling, tests or review checks you've built with them

  • Understand the security risks that agents bring, including prompt injection, over-broad permissions and untrusted dependencies

  • A developer-first outlook, where success looks like engineers choosing the secure option and owning their own security

  • Clear communicator who can turn security risk into practical decisions for technical and non-technical colleagues

We especially want to hear from you if you have:

  • Built security guardrails for teams working with coding agents or automated software delivery

  • Worked on software that serves many customers from shared infrastructure, and the data-separation questions that come with it

  • Worked in a functional language such as Haskell, or built security checks for a language the standard tools cover poorly

  • Worked in InsurTech, FinTech or another regulated industry

  • Helped build security practices from an early stage

  • Spent time training and coaching engineers on security

At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. We’re looking for a commercially sharp, highly autonomous operator to drive Axle’s commercial success in the French market.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are looking for a Senior People Operations Manager to own and improve the systems, processes and operational foundations behind our People function, across all of our markets.

Employee support

You will build the documentation, workflows, processes and self-service infrastructure that make the majority of standard People requests easy to solve without intervention, while personally handling the exceptions and escalations that genuinely require expertise.

About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

We are developing the flight control systems of our next-generation autonomous platforms, which are embedded and subjected to extreme operational constraints. As with any aeronautical system, no model is perfect: aerodynamic effects, actuator dynamics, wind, payload changes, damage or degraded sensors are never fully captured by the physics-based models we rely on.

These unmodelled dynamics are one of the main sources of performance loss and risk for a controller, especially at the edge of the flight envelope. To push the boundaries of control, we are working on estimating these disturbances online and compensating for them in real time through adaptive control and robust estimation.

Your mission

The goal of this internship is to design, implement and validate a framework for estimating and compensating unmodelled physics disturbances, in order to improve the robustness and performance of our flight controller in extreme and uncertain conditions.

Responsibilities

  • Literature review: Survey existing approaches to disturbance estimation and adaptive control

  • Algorithm implementation: Develop and implement the selected estimation and compensation algorithms within our simulation environment.

  • Performance evaluation: Assess and compare the performance and robustness of the developed methods against classical baselines.

  • Embedded constraints: Ensure the solutions are compatible with real-time execution and the computational limits of onboard hardware.

  • Documentation: Document all work performed, including methodologies, results and conclusions.

  • Flight test participation: Actively take part in flight test sessions to validate the developed algorithms in operational conditions, and contribute to their real-time deployment.

Candidates Requirements

  • Educational background: Strong academic record in automatic control, applied mathematics, or a related field. Knowledge of state estimation (Kalman filtering, observers) and nonlinear or adaptive control is a strong plus.

  • Technical skills: Solid understanding of control theory fundamentals and proficiency in Python or C++ is a plus. Experience with drones is a major plus.

  • Mindset: You are curious to learn, autonomous, rigorous and able to take initiative.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Platform Engineer – Maatwerk Software met Impact

Wij weten dat wat op het eerste gezicht eenvoudig lijkt, vaak complexer is dan men denkt. En wij begrijpen dat technologie geen barrière mag zijn, maar juist de verbinding naar een bestendige maatschappij. Bij Dawn Technology bouwen we niet zomaar digitale oplossingen. We ontwikkelen hoogwaardige maatwerk software die het leven van mensen verrijkt. Achter elke krachtige applicatie staat een stabiele en schaalbare cloudinfrastructuur. We maken geen compromissen op kwaliteit en zoeken altijd naar de best mogelijke oplossing, tot in de kleinste details. Om onze groeiambities te realiseren zoeken we een Platform Engineer. Iemand die zelfstandig complete IT-omgevingen ontwerpt, bouwt en automatiseert. Je pakt complexe migraties van A tot Z op en bouwt met visie aan een ijzersterk platform.

Jouw rol

Als Platform Engineer ben je verantwoordelijk voor het volledige proces van requirements tot oplevering. Je ontwerpt, bouwt en automatiseert moderne IT-infrastructuur voor uitdagende klantprojecten. Met tools zoals Terraform en Ansible til je onze automatisering naar het hoogste niveau. Je begeleidt complexe klantmigraties van A tot Z met oog voor detail. Daarnaast borg je een uitstekende overdracht en heldere documentatie voor je collega's. Zo creëer je voorspelbare, veilige en toekomstbestendige omgevingen voor maatschappelijk relevante organisaties.

Wat je zal gaan doen:

  • Ontwerpen en opbouwen van schaalbare IT-infrastructuur op basis van klantvereisten.

  • Automatiseren van omgevingen en processen met Terraform, Ansible en scripting.

  • Zelfstandig uitvoeren en begeleiden van complexe klantmigraties.

  • Inrichten van krachtige cloud- en Linux-omgevingen op platformen zoals Scaleway, AWS en Azure, volgens de nieuwste standaarden.

  • Opstellen van heldere documentatie en verzorgen van een vlekkeloze kennisoverdracht.

  • Waarborgen van de veiligheid, capaciteit en performance van het platform.

  • Adviseren van klanten en collega's over slimme infrastructurele keuzes.  

  • Na succesvolle oplevering draag je de omgeving over aan onze Hosting Engineers, die het dagelijkse beheer overnemen. Jij richt je vervolgens op het volgende project.


Wie ben jij?

We zoeken een ervaren professional met hbo werk- en denkniveau. Je voelt je thuis in Linux en Infrastructure as Code. Tools zoals Terraform en Ansible hebben voor jou geen geheimen: je bent echt een bouwer die zich als een vis in het water voelt bij deze technologieën. Je hebt ruime ervaring met het zelfstandig ontwerpen en migreren van complete IT-omgevingen. Je communiceert helder, pakt eigenaarschap en werkt gestructureerd. Verder woon je in Nederland en spreek je bij voorkeur Nederlands.

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • De Organisatie: Je versterkt een snelgroeiende, vooruitstrevende organisatie met een sterke visie en focus op maatschappelijk relevante software.

  • Autonomie: Je krijgt veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief, ondernemerschap en technische autonomie.

  • Maatschappelijke Impact: Je werkt aan uitdagende projecten met een directe en tastbare maatschappelijke impact.

  • Mobiliteit & Fiets: Een kilometervergoeding van € 0,25/km of een volledige OV-vergoeding, én een fiscaal aantrekkelijk fietsplan.

  • Pensioen: Een uitstekend en goed geregeld pensioen voor jouw toekomst.

  • Ontwikkeling & Extra's: Ruime mogelijkheden voor het volgen van opleidingen en trainingen om te blijven groeien, plus een jaarlijks Coolblue thuiswerkbudget van € 500,- om je werkplek perfect in te richten.

  • Events & Fun: Toffe (lokale) teamactiviteiten en gezellige, bedrijfsbrede Summer en Winter Events.

Over Dawn Technology

We bouwen niet voor de massa, maar voor betekenis. Onze klanten komen uit sectoren die er toe doen. Denk aan de zorg, educatie, duurzaamheid en publieke dienstverlening. We verstoppen complexiteit achter eenvoud. We bouwen software die logisch voelt. Precies dat maakt ons werk elke dag boeiend.

Samen met een groep van bijna 250 digitale specialisten delen we kennis. We zoeken de nieuwste technologieën op en versterken elkaar. Benieuwd naar de sfeer bij Dawn Technology? Luister dan eens naar deze podcast.

Solliciteren

Spreekt deze rol je aan? Laat je gegevens dan achter via de sollicitatieknop. Ook als je twijfelt of je volledig aansluit nodigen we je uit om te solliciteren. Nog vragen naar aanleiding van deze vacature? Neem dan gerust contact op met Dennis Timmerman (Corporate Recruiter) via 0638675360.

Have a great day. Dawn Technology.

    AIM Solutions is an early-stage deep-tech startup in Eindhoven building inspection and metrology equipment for the semiconductor industry. We are in an active build phase, small, and growing.

    You own how our tool is controlled and operated. The machine combines lasers, high-speed cameras, a nanometer-precision wafer stage and GPU-based image reconstruction.     You will:

    • Own the system control architecture: machine software, control hardware, timing and synchronization, and the data path from acquisition to reconstruction

    • Translate system performance and throughput goals into requirements for control, software and compute, and keep them traceable

    • Own the timing, throughput and data budgets, and decide where time is won or lost in a measurement

    • Define and guard the interfaces between control software, hardware and algorithms, including the hardware abstraction layer

    • Define how the machine is operated: machine states, sequencing, recipes, error handling, logging and monitoring

    • Steer the software and embedded engineers on the control side: set priorities, run design reviews and resolve trade-offs

    • Set up integration and verification of the control layer, with a test strategy that keeps it reliable as the hardware changes between builds

    • Carry the machine software from lab prototype toward a production tool that runs unattended in a fab

    • 8+ years in high-tech equipment, including several years as a system engineer, software architect or control architect for a complex machine

    • Experience with machine control in semiconductor, lithography, metrology or scientific instruments

    • Hands-on understanding of real-time and deterministic systems: hardware triggering, FPGA-based synchronization, motion control and high-rate data acquisition

    • Strong in equipment software architecture: layered designs, hardware abstraction, state machines and concurrency

    • Comfortable reading code and reviewing designs in Python and C/C++. You won’t write most of the code, but you can.

    • Strong in requirements, budgets and interface management across hardware and software

    • This is not a role in a large organization with fixed processes: you help decide how we work. You thrive in a small, fast-moving team where roles are fluid, and you are as likely to be at the lab bench debugging a trigger as in a design review.

    • A clear communicator with engineers, management and partners

    • Full professional proficiency in English

    Bonus:

    • Taking machine software from prototype to production, including SEMI standards for equipment communication and automation (such as SECS/GEM) and machine safety

    • Integration with wafer handling and factory automation

    • High-throughput data pipelines or GPU computing

    • Experience with optical or imaging systems: cameras, lasers, image data

    • Model-based systems engineering or modern requirements tools

    We care more about systems thinking and ownership than about a perfect match. If your title was software architect, control architect or lead engineer, but you have owned how a complex machine runs, apply anyway.

    What we offer

    • Shared technical leadership of a tool that does not exist anywhere else yet

    • Small team, short feedback loops, real impact on the product

    • Competitive salary for the Dutch market

Vividly is the leading modern trade promotion management (TPM) solution built by and for the consumer packaged goods industry. From campaign creation to deductions management and promotion measurement, we help brands manage every element of trade spend. With our easy-to-use platform and industry-leading experience, we pride ourselves on our ability to bring businesses to the next level.

Not familiar with trade promotion spend? That’s OK. Most people aren’t. It’s an $8 trillion dollar problem that is ripe for disruption by an innovative SaaS startup. In order to grow, consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands spend 20% of their topline revenue to get into retailers and promote their products within those retailers. The problem is that today 70% of those promotions are not ROI positive. This is because ROI is hard to track. The industry operates on emails, pdfs, and xls spreadsheets. At Vividly, we’re solving this massive problem with exciting tactics including AI, Machine Learning, and Fintech and adding value to everyone in the chain. Some of our customers include brands you may use and love - Liquid Death, Amy’s, and Perfect Snacks.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for an Account Executive who brings both SaaS sales expertise and a deep understanding of the CPG ecosystem. This is a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of technology, finance, and commercial strategy - selling a high-impact solution into organizations where trade spend directly influences revenue, margin, and growth. You will own the full sales cycle, lead complex, multi-stakeholder deals, and partner with senior leaders across Sales, Finance, and Operations to drive meaningful business outcomes.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the full sales cycle - from prospecting through close - focused on acquiring new CPG customers
  • Build and manage a pipeline through outbound prospecting, self-sourcing, and collaboration with SDR and Marketing teams
  • Lead consultative discovery to uncover inefficiencies in trade spend, promotions, and revenue execution
  • Translate customer challenges into quantified business value (e.g., ROI improvement, margin expansion, revenue lift)
  • Navigate and align cross-functional buying groups, including Sales, Finance, Revenue Management, and Operations
  • Drive complex, multi-threaded deals with multiple stakeholders and decision-makers
  • Deliver tailored, value-based presentations that clearly articulate Vividly’s impact
  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Marketing, and Customer Success to ensure long-term customer value
  • Consistently exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets through disciplined pipeline management

Who You Are

You are a consultative, value-driven seller who thrives in complex environments and understands how large organizations make decisions.

You bring a strong grasp of how CPG businesses operate and can confidently engage stakeholders across both commercial and financial functions. You are equally comfortable discussing margin impact with Finance as you are with execution challenges with Sales teams.

You are resourceful, proactive, and motivated by solving real business problems - not just closing deals.

What We’re Looking For

Required

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying experience in SaaS sales, with a track record of closing complex, multi-threaded deals
  • Experience working in or selling into the CPG industry (brand, broker, retailer, or distributor ecosystem)
  • Proven ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders, including Director, VP, and C-level executives
  • Strong experience with consultative sales methodologies (e.g., MEDDIC, Challenger, SPIN, Sandler, or similar)
  • Demonstrated success in outbound prospecting and building pipeline independently
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and storytelling skills

Highly Preferred

  • Experience with trade promotion, revenue management, retail execution, or deductions workflows
  • Background selling data, analytics, or financial SaaS solutions
  • Familiarity with TPM, TPO, or adjacent systems
  • Experience selling into Finance or RevOps functions

Why This Role Is Different

  • Sell into a mission-critical problem: Trade spend is one of the largest and least optimized investments in CPG
  • Engage at the executive level: Work directly with leaders responsible for revenue, margin, and growth
  • Operate in a complex, strategic sales environment: Multi-stakeholder deals with real business impact
  • Define a category: Be part of modernizing trade promotion management—not selling a commoditized solution
  • Leverage your domain expertise: Your CPG knowledge is not a “nice-to-have”—it’s a competitive advantage

Compensation Range:

Base salary: $ 100,000 per year

On-Target Earnings (OTE): $200,000 per year

This information reflects the anticipated base salary range for this position, based on current national and/or regional market data. Minimums and maximums may vary by geography. Individual pay will be determined by factors such as skills, experience, and role relevance. In addition, for this role you will be eligible for On-Target Earnings (OTE): the total compensation you can expect if you achieve 100% of your sales targets (base salary + commission/bonus) — a common practice in sales compensation. Your actual earnings may vary depending on performance, quota attainment, ramp period, and other factors.

Why Choose Vividly?

A modern, remote-first workplace

We are committed to succeeding as a fully remote team, empowering you with the flexibility to thrive, no commute required. Every Vividly team member receives a stipend upon hire to help create a comfortable and productive home office.

Vividly days off & flexible PTO

For most USA holidays that fall on a Monday or Friday, we turn it into a 4 day weekend! Vividly also offers Flexible Time Off (and we really mean it) to help prevent burn out and fuel creativity.

Competitive Benefits

  • Healthcare, Dental and Vision - We cover 100% of your monthly premiums and 50% of all dependents
  • 401(k) - With a 3% employer contribution
  • Weekly $20 Sharebite Meal Stipend - For every meal you purchase, they donate a meal through Feeding America!
  • Monthly $50 Wellness Reimbursement
  • Monthly $200 Remote Work Stipend

Commitment to our values - The Vividly Code

  • Kind Ambition -We push boundaries with empathy and integrity
  • Keep It Real - We are transparent, honest, and authentic
  • Customer Love - We act as trusted advisors to our customers

  • Urgency Wins - We move quickly and focus on impact
